thread:
incident-bot: Paging @maria-sre @tao-sre @sam-security — auth-api cluster: sudden spike of token validation successes from unknown IPs followed by abnormal object reads from logs-bucket. possible leaked session tokens. auto-detect flagged 1500 requests in 4m. severity: high :rotating_light:

maria-sre: saw the page, jumping on. tagging infra for quick triage. where's the raw?

incident-bot: Alert details: rule=auth.session.surge, cluster=auth-prod-1, first_seen=1980012338, src_ips=[45.76.12.9, 45.76.12.10, 203.0.113.45], sample_path=/api/v1/sessions/validate, user_agent=python-requests/2.31.0, potential_files_accessed=logs/debug-2026-03-15.tar.gz

sam-security: if those IPs map to known hosters we should assume creds are leaked. immediate actions: 1) rotate service tokens 2) revoke active sessions 3) block IPs at edge 4) preserve disk and network captures.

alex-eng: I'm pulling the auth logs now. running quick grep for the IPs, will paste findings.

alex-eng: ```
# auth-proxy logs (excerpt)
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z auth-prod-1 user=svc-ingest action=validate token_id=svc-abc123 status=200 src=45.76.12.9 path=/api/v1/sessions/validate
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z auth-prod-1 user=svc-ingest action=get_object object=logs/debug-2026-03-15.tar.gz status=200 src=45.76.12.9
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z auth-prod-1 user=svc-ingest action=validate token_id=svc-abc123 status=200 src=45.76.12.10
```

maria-sre: that token_id looks like a long-lived service token. tao, can you run `kubectl get secret svc-ingest -n prod -o yaml` and check where it's mounted? we need to find scope and rotate.

tao-sre: on it. also putting WAF rule to block 45.76.12.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 at the edge (cloudfront/waf). will push now.

tao-sre: waf rule deployed: rule-id=waf-rot-93, blocking 45.76.12.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24. propagated to all edges.

sam-security: coordinating token rotation — plan: force rotate svc-ingest, revoke all sessions issued with that token, rotate JWT signing key if we see user tokens minted using it. tagging @sec-bot to run rotation automation.

sec-bot: Received rotation job request. executing: rotate-service-token --service svc-ingest --force --reason "suspected leak 1980012345"

sec-bot: Rotation step 1 complete: new token issued (redacted). step 2: pushing new secret to k8s (prod) and triggering rollout of auth-proxy pods.

maria-sre: rolling restart in progress for auth-proxy; pods will pick up new secret. rolling restart command:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-proxy -n prod
```

alex-eng: applied restart, watching readiness. also created a temporary denylist rule in auth-proxy to refuse any requests with token_id=svc-abc123.

alex-eng: denylist snippet pushed:
```
if token_id == "svc-abc123": return 401
```

sam-security: good. preserve forensic evidence: tao, start packet capture on auth-prod-1 for next 2h. snapshot disks on instances that saw access. create AMIs.

tao-sre: started tcpdump (saved to s3 forensic-bucket/session-1980012345.pcap) and kicked off disk snapshot jobs (snapshots queued).

amy-cs: wondering about customer impact — which customers touched those logs? do we have any PII in that archive? prepping communication but need confirmed scope. cc @maria-sre

maria-sre: initial list: internal debug logs and some request traces; not expected to contain full PII but may have user_ids and truncated emails in traces. security to confirm. amy, prepare draft that doesn't call out specifics yet.

sam-security: security triage: run quick grep for personal data patterns in the archived file object names. also checking access logs to see any targeted customer IDs.

alex-eng: found accesses to s3://redwood-logs/debug-archives/logs-debug-2026-03-15.tar.gz by svc-ingest from those IPs between 09:12:03 and 09:12:10. object size ~120MB. extracting list of files now.

alex-eng: ```
# s3 ls output (excerpt)
logs-debug-2026-03-15/
logs-debug-2026-03-15/request_traces/trace-001.json
logs-debug-2026-03-15/request_traces/trace-002.json
logs-debug-2026-03-15/debug-metrics.txt
logs-debug-2026-03-15/potentially-sensitive/diagnostic-session-uuids.txt
```

sam-security: prioritize the request_traces files — get a sanitized sample to verify if real emails/PII are present. alex, can you pull trace-001.json and grep for @ or email patterns?

alex-eng: grabbed trace-001.json, doing quick grep. result: 2 occurrences of email-like strings, both masked partially (e.g., user+...@example.com). attaching sample to secure channel.

sam-security: that's borderline. escalate to legal/org if we see clear full emails or identifiers. for now treat as potential impact. amy, draft a holding notice for affected customers and set a follow-up window: 24 hours.

amy-cs: draft ready, will wait for go from maria/sam before send.

maria-sre: next ops: 1) confirm all svc-ingest tokens rotated across all environments 2) revoke active sessions referencing svc-abc123 3) ensure new tokens no longer accept old ones 4) monitor for any replay from other IPs 5) schedule postmortem. assigning owners: rotate=sec-bot/tao-sre, revoke=auth-admins, monitoring=maria-sre, comms=amy-cs.

sec-bot: Rotation audit: svc-ingest rotated in prod, staging, and ops. old token marked revoked. revocation-ids: rv-198a, rv-198b.

oncall-placeholder: auth-admins run `authctl revoke --token-id svc-abc123 --all-sessions` and confirm.

alex-eng: revoke command executed, returned: {"revoked_sessions": 112, "revoked_tokens": 3} (redacted).

maria-sre: monitoring dashboards — token validation rate for svc-ingest dropped to baseline after denylist + rotate. edge blocking cut off the external IPs. continuing to watch for 2h.

sam-security: open tasks for follow-up: - forensics packet analysis - search for other exported archives in last 7 days - audit service account key rotation cadence and reduce token TTLs - enforce least privilege for svc-ingest

amy-cs: sending holding notice now to affected customers: template includes general statement about suspicious access, mitigations, and promise to update in 24 hours.

maria-sre: thanks team. switching to incident review channel in 30m. leaving thread open for any late indicators.

sam-security: adding retrospective: rotate all long-lived service tokens to ephemeral tokens within 90d and add automated detection for object reads tied to token validation spikes.

incident-bot: Incident triage update recorded: incident_id=INC-1980012345, status=mitigated->monitoring, paged=3 oncall recipients, runbook=runbooks/incident-auth-exfil.md, severity=high

maria-sre: handing off to monitoring shift @tao-sre for the next 2 hours. tao take it.

tao-sre: acked, taking watch. will escalate if new IPs or replays show up.

amy-cs: will wait for 24h confirmation before external detailed notice. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
